answer.rationale: Write-path latency at 5x target is confined to the primary region, so moving traffic to the standby region removes the degraded node while keeping the new security-patch release (no rollback needed) and keeping customer writes flowing. Regional failover is the only candidate that isolates a primary-region fault without touching the non-revertible release, and it fits the one-shot intervention window. Capacity add would be slower and wouldn't help if the cause is a regional infra issue; read replicas only offload reads, not the write path; circuit breakers are for dependency outages, not internal latency; rollback is ruled out by compliance.
